# Red team — `design-after-midpoint-review.md` and `PLAN.md`

**2026-09-21 · one read-only Opus analyst · no file in the repository or any worktree was
changed.** Scripts at
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kentgang-git3-katalyst/b70a1857-a894-4bbe-b3a6-4d7cf3ebc4f8/scratchpad/digest/redteam/`
(`rt_core.py`, `attack1.py`…`attack4.py`). I ran no paid call, no server, no whole suite, no
playwright. **PROVED** means I ran it or read it; **SUSPECT** means I argued it and did not
measure it. Every number below is mine unless I say otherwise.

---

## 1. Verdict

**Sound with changes — but three of them are load-bearing and one is a straight error of
fact.** The engine reformulation is the right idea, the hazard model is right, the collapse
from event *times* to event *truths* is a genuinely good trade, and `Suppose this is true` comes
out exact to four decimal places; I could not break that. What is not true is the word
**exact**: under `This happened` the design does exact arithmetic on a table built from the
wrong timing, and I measured **0.124** of error on a four-claim map — twenty-five times the
worst gap the design quotes, on the product's second verb. Separately, `sustain` does not
survive §2.2 — so the event/state split is **required**, not optional, and the decision put to
Kent as a free choice is not one; and the cost line ("3 sessions, net −350 lines") is scoped to
the one file where the work is cheapest and omits `diff.py`, the browser, 60 tests and ~400
lines of spec.

---

## 2. Must change before Kent sees it

### M1. "Solved exactly" is false under *This happened*. The design must say so and state a tolerance. — **PROVED**

The design (§2.2): *"Whether each claim happens is then solved exactly … `This happened`
multiplies in the evidence and renormalises. Both exact."* The arithmetic is exact. **The table
it is applied to is not**, and an observation is exactly the operation that invalidates it.

The forward pass produces each claim's arrival-time distribution **under the prior**. Evidence
moves a claim's arrival as well as its truth ("if B happened, A more likely happened early"),
and the design never rebuilds the tables. `do` is fine, because the design explicitly re-runs
the forward pass under it. `observe` is not.

I wrote a faithful implementation of §2.2 (`rt_core.py`) and an exact-over-times reference,
with **all three arrow shapes** — the analyst's scripts use `step` only; the string `shape`
never appears in `ve_cost.py`, `pin_error.py` or `pin_error_many.py`, so the quoted .0065 and
.049 have never met an `impulse`, the one shape where timing is everything.

Worst |design − exact| by map family (`attack1.py`, K = 24):

| map | worst gap | where |
|---|---|---|
| the analyst's own map, my code (control) | .0022 | — |
| impulse, short half-life, near a deadline | .0001 | *(the design is fine here — see below)* |
| diamond, equal lags | .0055 | observe |
| chain, depth 6 / depth 10 | .0090 / .0109 | observe |
| diamond, lags 2 vs 34 | .0125 | observe |
| **strong inhibitor** | **.0229** | observe |
| **lag 26 days against a 28-day gap** | **.0338** | observe |
| **"race against the clock" chain, lag 9 of a 12-day gap** | **.0352** | observe |

**Every gap over .01 is an observation.** Over 140 adversarially generated four-claim maps
(`attack2.py` §B, tight deadlines, lags up to 70 % of each gap, mixed shapes — 9 520 compared
numbers):

| query | n | mean | p99 | worst | **share off by more than .005** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no edit | 560 | .00027 | .0046 | .0175 | 0.9 % |
| `do` (Suppose) | 4 480 | .00007 | .0015 | .0259 | **0.2 %** |
| `observe` (This happened) | 4 480 | .00127 | .0151 | **.2043** | **6.6 %** |

The worst case re-run at a finer grid is **not** a grid artefact: at K = 40 it is **.1242**
(exact .6318, design .5076), stable. Its shape: three parents, impulse arrows with long lags,
and an observation on a claim that is *also* a parent of another parent — so the evidence
shifts the second parent's arrival and the table never learns. In-degree 3 is what generation
is built to produce; 3 of the 19 arrows in the committed recording are `impulse`.

**The mechanism, stated so it can be checked:** the error needs the evidence to move a
*parent's arrival time*. A plain chain A→R→M observed at R is exact to four places
(`attack3.py` §A) because "R happened" gives back exactly R's prior arrival conditional on
happening. It is when the evidence reaches a claim through two routes that the cut
approximation bites.

**There is no cheap patch.** I tried the obvious one — rebuild the tables from the arrival
distributions the exact model has *after* conditioning, then redo the same truth solve. It
double-counts the evidence and makes the gap **worse**: on the lag-26 map, +.0338 becomes
+.0581; on the race chain, +.0352 becomes +.0501 (`attack2.py` §C).

**Concrete edit.** In §2.2, replace *"Both exact"* with: *"`Suppose` is exact. `This happened`
is exact arithmetic on a table built from the prior's timing; measured against exact-over-times
it is within .005 on most maps and can reach .12 when the evidence reaches a claim by two
routes through impulse arrows."* Then pick one and write it down: (a) accept it and set the
displayed tolerance accordingly, or (b) rebuild the forward pass under evidence by iterating to
a fixed point, and cost it. Do not ship a screen that says two significant figures next to an
engine whose second figure moves.

### M2. PLAN 05-1's oracle cannot catch a wrong table. Here is the test that can. — **PROVED by construction**

PLAN 05-1: *"a brute-force enumerator over ≤5-claim maps asserting every number to 1e-9 against
the exact core."* At `1e-9` there are only two possibilities, and both are bad: either the
enumerator builds the same yes/no tables the core does — in which case it proves the variable
elimination is right and is **blind to everything in M1** — or it builds them independently,
in which case it cannot pass at `1e-9` at all and the tolerance gets loosened until it does.
Either way the timing approximation is invisible, and the project's headline test would be
certifying the one thing that is wrong.

**Write two tests, with two tolerances, proving two different things.**

1. **`test_the_elimination_is_exact`** — tolerance `1e-9`. The enumerator takes **the core's own
   yes/no tables** and sums the 2ⁿ joint by hand, applying `do` as a point mass and `observe` as
   a mask-and-renormalise. This proves the elimination, the `do` surgery and the conditioning.
   Cheap, fast, and it is what 05-1 actually describes.
2. **`test_the_tables_agree_with_integrating_over_time`** — tolerance **measured, not aspirational**.
   The enumerator is forbidden the core's tables and is built **from the arrow parameters alone**
   (`q0`, `q1`, `lag`, `shape`, `half_life`, the deadline): it enumerates the full
   `(K+1)ⁿ` first-passage joint at a fine grid for n ≤ 4, conditions there, and reports
   `1 − P(never)`. This is the only test that can see M1. It must run `do` **and** `observe`,
   and it must include an impulse arrow and a diamond, because a step-shaped chain does not
   reproduce the defect. `rt_core.exact_over_times` is a working 80-line version of this
   enumerator; it is in the scratchpad and can be lifted.

Set test 2's tolerance from a measured sweep and **write the number in the record**, so that if
someone later tightens the model the test tells them.

### M3. `sustain` does not survive §2.2. The event/state split is required, and the decision Kent is being offered is not a real choice. — **PROVED**

Today (`propagation.py:1431-1434`) a `sustain` arrow pushes with `truth[source]` — the source's
truth **read on every day** — and a `trigger` arrow with `fired[source]`, one flag per world.
They differ only because today a claim can **un-resolve** when an impulse fades
(`propagation.py:1444`) — which is defect E5, the thing §2.2 removes on purpose.

Under first passage `truth[source]` on day *t* is exactly `1 if τ_source ≤ t`, which is
monotone and absorbing. So a `sustain` arrow pushes from `τ_source + lag` onward — and so does
a `trigger` arrow with the same `shape` and `lag`. I built both: identical to six decimal
places (`attack3.py` §B). **`mode` becomes dead data, fully determined by `shape`.** And the
one mechanism that can un-true a claim today — automatic retraction — is precisely what record
0017 deletes. ADR-0005 calls `trigger`/`sustain` *"the best idea in the brainstorm"*
(`docs/adr/0005:72`).

So §2.3's framing — *"offered to Kent as OPTIONAL … the engine does not depend on it"* — is
wrong in the way that matters. §2.2 does not merely leave `sustain` unimproved; it **deletes**
it. The design's own parenthetical half-sees this (*"this split may be required by §2.2, not
optional"*) and then the sentence beside it says the engine lands either way. Both cannot be true.

**And a state is not one yes/no variable.** A state holds over an interval; its children read
the hazard integrated over that interval. Four maps in which "did it ever hold?" is YES in every
row, differing only in when the state switched on and off, give the child **.148, .193, .215,
.827** (`attack3.py` §C) — 0.68 of probability spread across maps a single bit cannot tell
apart. A state claim in the binary network therefore needs **two** times, on and off, and its
"truth" variable has to be *defined* ("holds at the deadline"? "ever held"? they are different
questions and the tile sentence must say which).

**Concrete edits.** (i) In §2.3, move event/state out of "three things that ride with it" and
into §2.2 as a consequence, with the honest sentence: *"`mode` no longer does anything on its
own. Either claims split into events and states, or `sustain` is deleted from the vocabulary and
`shape` carries the whole distinction."* (ii) Say what a state claim's number means, in one
sentence, before any code. (iii) Offer Kent the cheap third option nobody has written down:
**keep events only and express a sustained push as two arrows** — one from the onset event and
an inhibitor from the ending event. That reproduces `sustain` exactly under first passage, costs
a validity rule and a prompt sentence instead of a wire field and a schema change, and it is the
option that does *not* move the fingerprint twice. (iv) Re-cost: the engine digest prices
event/state at 1.3 sessions *on top of* §2.2's three, and §2.2's "3 sessions" does not include it.

### M4. `series` cannot keep its meaning, and the design says it does. — **PROVED**

§2.2's "Kept untouched" list includes *"the `World` and `Diff` shapes the browser reads"*, and
the engine digest spells out that `series` *"keeps its type and its meaning"*. It cannot.

Today `series` is an **instantaneous** per-day likelihood that is explicitly allowed to fall.
`tests/unit/fixtures/test_hormuz_golden.py:117-120` pins it:

```
assert strike.series["H"][0] == 1.0
assert 0.25 < strike.series["H"][1] < 0.45
assert strike.series["H"][1] == strike.series["H"][3]
assert strike.series["H"][4] < 0.10
```

`1.0 → .36 → .36 → <.10`. Under *"the chance it happens by day t"* the series is a cumulative
curve: **monotone non-decreasing, never falling.** `1.0 → .36` is arithmetically impossible.
`test_hormuz_golden.py:81` also pins `series["B"][1] < series["B"][2]` after a fall. This is the
largest unadmitted change in the proposal and it is hiding inside the field the design was most
confident about. It takes `DeltaRow.peak_delta` and `at_day` with it — their whole rationale
("shows up for a fortnight and then unwinds") presumes a curve that can unwind.

**It also answers the red-team question about a dated observation.** Under *This happened on
day 5* the coherent per-day object is `P(τ ≤ t | evidence)` — which the design **can** state,
but only if the yes/no variable is re-cut per day, and that is a different (and larger) object
than the single "by its deadline" variable §2.2 describes. The design says *"every displayed day
rides along as an array axis"* and never says what the axis holds. **Decide this before the
first line of code**, and note the related contradiction: §2.2 says the forward pass runs at
*"12–24 points"*, the engine digest says *"~180 displayed days"* ride as elimination axes
(`propagation.py:110`, `SERIES_CAP = 180`). Those are different engines with different costs.

### M5. "3 sessions, net −350 lines" is scoped to the easiest file. Five to seven is the floor. — **PROVED**

`propagation.py` is 1 831 lines: 782 strictly executable, 847 docstring. "−1 100" is more lines
than the file has executable. What the estimate forgot:

- **`diff.py` (611 executable lines).** `versions_of`, `Versions`, `counting_for`,
  `_moved_only_by_reweighting`, `_agreement_on`'s weighting, `_width_of_the_band`'s `_band`
  import, `_worlds_do_not_match`, and `sensitivity`'s reconstruction of `introduced_by` from
  `world.retractions` all die or change. `_ranked_endings` reads `world.series` — so M4 lands in
  the one place §2.2 promised was untouched.
- **The browser, budgeted at zero.** §2.2 says the wire is kept; §2.3 of the same page budgets
  *"−120 browser"*. `moved_only_by_reweighting` has two rendering readers
  (`Inspector.tsx:248`, `graph/diff/noChange.ts:52`); `retractions` feeds the
  `Retracted · date · by "…"` badge whose height is baked into `geometry.ts` and `Tile.tsx`;
  `apiSource.ts:228` prints *"8 worlds under each"* in the provenance sentence, which becomes a
  false statement about an engine with no inner loop.
- **The `p = 1.0` on a supposed claim.** The digest calls the path product *"its only reader"*.
  It is not: `diff.py:817-818` reads it for every `ClaimDiff.before/after`, `diff.py:460` reads
  it to choose the flip direction in `sensitivity`, and `apiSource.ts:263` builds a `Belief`
  from it. `Belief.p` forbids `None`. Removing it is a wire break.
- **Tests.** 60 of 462 backend test functions touch the dying machinery — **34 of
  `test_propagation.py`'s 46**. "−300 lines" understates it, and the real cost is not deletion
  but re-derivation: `spec/multiverse/propagation.md` carries **239** numeric literals and
  `diff.md` **166**, all of which move at once.
- **The locality oracle gets harder, not free.** `test_patches.py:1211` and the
  `GraphEditMachine` state machine hand-roll `_observation_reach`'s rule (`_affected_from_the_shape`,
  `_evidence_moved`, ~46 lines). Under exact elimination that rule becomes d-separation, so the
  oracle must be rewritten — and §2.2's claim that *"locality becomes a theorem"* means it should
  get **stricter**.
- **The comparable.** `d9c853e` (#38) fixed **one** defect class, preserved every wire meaning,
  and cost 1 335 insertions across 12 files with 400 lines of churn in `propagation.py`. This
  change is ~3.4× that in `propagation.py` alone, plus a `diff.py` rewrite, plus deleting a wire
  model with live browser readers, plus 300–400 spec lines instead of 44.

### M6. "Pay once" does not survive 05-2 → 05-4. At least three fingerprint moves land after the paid re-record. — **PROVED**

The fingerprint is `sha256(STANDING_TEXT + json(what_goes_out()))` (`engine/prompt.py:154-185`);
the response schemas are ~80 % of its input, so any new field moves it. Measured on `main`:
`1c224cc3…`, byte-identical to the recording's header. Measured with `persistence` added to
`ClaimProposal`: `1e80b47b…` — **changed**.

Landing after the single $5 re-record:

1. **`persistence: event | state`** (PLAN 05-4). No code in `domain/` can read a claim's sentence
   and decide whether it names an event or a state — that is what the model is for. And it is
   not hypothetical: the committed `hormuz.jsonl` has **19 arrows, 6 of them `sustain`, and all
   six leave claims of kind `event`**. With `persistence` defaulting to `event` and the new
   validity rule in force, all six become illegal. **`persistence` belongs in 05-2** — which
   means record 0017 must be *accepted* before the freeze is written, not merged alongside it.
2. **`q₁`'s timing clause.** The hazard calibration requires "the cause happens at the start of
   the window" (`review2/repro/hazard_prototype.py:6,20`). Design §4's `LinkDraft` dropped it.
   One sentence now; a second re-record if it is discovered at the flip.
3. **The claim's own prior, restated as the leak.** The prompt asks for a marginal
   (`prompt.py:96-98`, `:250-253`, `:306-307`; `proposal.py:78-82`) and the code has always
   consumed it as a leak (`propagation.py:1427`). The exact core needs it to be a leak
   *explicitly*. Prompt text, free now.

Also: **05-2's "no search on the first call" moves `tool_choice`, which is outside the
fingerprint but inside the cassettes' `match_on: [… body]`.** It breaks all eight cassettes,
leaves the hash green, and makes `hormuz.jsonl` a recording of behaviour the program no longer
has — the exact silent-staleness the hash was introduced to prevent
(`spec/generation/replay.md:223`). And if 05-2 merges before the new `.jsonl` does, the
`recordings` CI job is red on `main`, against the always-green rule. Record on the branch;
commit the recording in the same pull request.

### M7. The `q₀`/`q₁` wording is not a specification, and the interim derivation is wrong for `impulse` arrows. — **PROVED**

Design §4 elicits `p_effect_if_cause` / `p_effect_if_not_cause` with two comments. For a claim
with three causes they are ambiguous three ways: (a) what the *other* causes are doing is
unstated — "if the cause happens" invites a marginalised conditional, which is not what either
engine's calibration takes; (b) `q₀` is elicited once **per arrow**, so three arrows into one
claim yield three numbers that must all be equal, and a fourth (the claim's `prior`) that must
equal them too, with nothing enforcing it; (c) *when* the cause happens is unstated.

The only reading both engines can consume: **`q₀` = P(effect by its own deadline | none of the
causes on this map happens)** — a property of the *claim*, not the arrow, and identical to its
`prior`; **`q₁` = P(effect by that same deadline | this cause happens on the first day of the
window and no other cause on the map happens)**.

And the interim derivation does not hold. With `strength = logit(q₁) − logit(q₀)` on today's
engine, measured: `step` lag 0 → .7000 ✓, `step` lag 30 → .7000 ✓, `ramp` → .7000 ✓,
**`impulse` lag 7 half-life 14 → .2000 ✗** (the elicited `q₁` of .70 is discarded entirely; the
spike has faded by the day the claim is read). **3 of 19 arrows in the committed recording are
`impulse`.** So the same two elicited numbers mean measurably different things before and after
05-4 — which is a second reason to pin the window in the prompt, not the shape.

Also: the "free coherence check" (`p_child ≈ p_parent·q₁ + (1−p_parent)·q₀`) contradicts
"our code sets the leak to `q₀`". If `p_child` is the leak the residual is `p_parent·(q₁−q₀)`,
nonzero by construction on every arrow that does anything. 05-2 freezes neither reading and
never mentions `prior`.

### M8. Things stated as fact that are not true. — **PROVED**

| Stated | Actually |
|---|---|
| §4: *"The map has no arrow that pushes down **because the prompt never asks. The words are not in it.**"* | They are in it. `engine/proposal.py:164-171`, the `strength` description, shipped in the fingerprinted payload: *"negative less likely… −1 cuts them to a third."* And a `.runs/` generation with **no insert** drew three negative arrows. This is the stated reason for a prompt change inside the paid batch. |
| §1.2: *"**No test compares the engine with an independently computed answer**"* | `test_propagation.py:1172` does, for the band, by an independent delta method. The true claim is narrower: *no oracle covers `p`, and no oracle runs under an edit* — which is still the finding that matters. |
| §5: *"`App.tsx` **1 524 → 483** lines"* | `main` is **1 074**, and so is the merge base. 483 is right; the reduction claimed is about double the real one. |
| §2.4: *"812 lines of code"*; §2.4: *"31 executable lines"* (`_two_figures`); §6: *"547 decimals in 13 files"*; §4: *"55 tokens a second"*; §6: *"~43 000 words"* | 782 strictly executable (839 counting comments); `_two_figures` is **20** executable of 101; no decimal count by any method gives 547-in-13 (819 in `spec/` alone); the receipt gives **78.7** tok/s; Data-model sections total **35 133** words. |
| §2.2: *"All **200** versions"* | The code is **2 000** (`engine/worlds.py:63`, `propagation.py:385`), and ADR-0014 §B specifies 2 000 × 8. If 200 is a new parameter, say so — it currently reads as a description of today. |
| §3: *"in **five** files"* (the .61/.48 fixture contradiction) | **Six**, and `hormuz.py:298` already self-corrects while `:284` in the same file still asserts the old number. |
| §6: *"About **twenty** workbench passages still say 'in this stack there is no engine'"* | **One** passage says it (`spec/workbench/keyboard-and-access.md:223`). The other ~17 hits are live product copy — `kind: "no_engine"`, `words: "no engine yet"` — shipping today in `App.tsx:267,287,297`. A sweep would delete correct vocabulary. |

### M9. The document that unblocks the plan does not exist. — **PROVED**

`PLAN.md:3` — *"PROPOSED until Kent answers `notes/2026-09-21-decisions-after-review.md`"*.
`find` returns nothing. With PRD anti-pattern 13 (*"Do not implement against a `proposed`
decision record"*, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md:229`), **no session of 05/06/07 is startable.**
Writing that document is on the critical path and is scheduled nowhere.

### M10. Stack 07 schedules something FR-8 forbids verbatim. — **PROVED**

`PLAN.md:58` — *"a small ensemble for numbers"*. `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md:115` — *"**No
ensemble in v1**: no claim is asked about twice"*, reopened by *one* condition: FR-30's
pastcast. `PLAN.md:64` cuts the pastcast. The only key to that lock is thrown away in the same
document. ADR-0015 forbids it too. Cut it, or amend FR-8 and ADR-0015 in 07-0.

---

## 3. Should change

**S1. 05-4 bundles four independent risks into one pull request** — the flag flip (every number
changes), a schema change (`persistence`), an invariant rewrite (INV-8), and a wire change
(`Observe.at`). The engine digest staged these as **three separate pull requests** (§7, PRs 3,
4, 5). PLAN merged them and lost the staging that kept `main` safe. It is also the single gate
on three quarters of stack 06 (06-2 → 06-3 → 06-4 → all of 07), so **a one-session slip in 05-4
is a one-session slip in the finish date**. Nothing else has that property.

**S2. The `Draws` contract is not the clean decoupling it is sold as. — SUSPECT, resting on a PROVED premise.**
§3's `Draws{when, weight}` is called *"the ONLY coupling to the engine"*, and 06-2's first-touch
stop/target reads `when`. But the design produces `when` by drawing truths from the exact
posterior and then drawing times **forward under the prior's conditionals**. Under an
observation those times are wrong in exactly the way M1 measures — the arrival distribution
after conditioning is not the prior's, and the design never computes it. So "first touch on a
daily price path" inherits the one approximation the design does not bound, and it lands on the
number the reader trades on. Two consequences: (i) `weight` should not be documented as *"all
ones from an exact sampler"* without saying which distribution the times came from; (ii) the
claim that the two stacks do not wait on each other is weaker than stated, because the producer
of `Draws` is the forward sampler 05-4 replaces. I did not measure the stop-probability error.

**S3. "Their files are disjoint" is false at three points.** 05-4 re-derives Hormuz and 06-3
carries *"the fixture's six honest fixes"* — both `fixtures/hormuz.py`. 05-4 deletes the
retraction badge (−120 browser), 06-4 rewrites the same tiles, and 04-polish is editing the
Inspector and panel concurrently — three pull requests on `Tile.tsx`/`BranchPanel.tsx`, against
PLAN's own *"one agent per file-owning area"*.

**S4. ~19 sessions is about 1.6× optimistic; bottom-up it is ~31.** Using the analysts' own
per-item costs: stack-04 tail ≈ 6.5 (PLAN calls it *"small"*), 05 ≈ 9.5 (claimed 7), 06 ≈ 7.7
(claimed 7 — the best-calibrated number in the plan), 07 ≈ 7 without the gates and ≈ 10 with
(claimed 5, while one gated item inside it is *"about 3 sessions"*). The true serial critical
path is ≈ 20.75 sessions; the advertised 05/06 overlap buys only 06-0 and 06-1 — about 2.5
sessions — off it. There is no historical session accounting anywhere in the repo to calibrate
against, so these are first numbers; say so. And the per-pull-request Opus review that *"found a
must-fix on every branch of this stack"* is now policy and is in none of the estimates.

**S5. Best cuts the plan fails to make** (≈ 5.5–6.5 sessions, almost all in 07): the
one-streamed-call skeleton (**3 sessions**, 60 % of stack 07, and the design's own §4 says the
quality case for it *"is gone"* and the demo runs from a recording anyway); the ensemble (M10);
`Release` (undo an edit — in no brief clause, no FR, no invariant, and it is a domain + wire +
generated-types change smuggled into a browser pull request). **Do not cut** *the other three
recordings* — it is the one gated item the brief actually demands (`ASSIGNMENT.md:22-29`, four
named inputs; FR-3 is P0), at $15 and two hours, and it is the cheapest brief-coverage item in
the plan.

**S6. Three small holes in coverage.** (i) **FR-31 (P0) is nowhere** — not built
(`ARCHITECTURE.md:173`, *"Nothing is stored yet"*), not in any stack, not in NOT DOING.
(ii) Record 0019 amends INV-14/FR-23/FR-24 but not **FR-22** and does not mention **PRD
anti-pattern 11** (*"Do not type the stop-loss by hand"*), which it directly reverses — the
finance analyst found this and it was dropped on the way into PLAN. (iii) Six functional
requirements are cut with **no record at all** (FR-17, FR-18, FR-20, FR-24 partly, FR-29,
FR-30) while the definition of done requires *"every decision has an accepted record"*.
Also: the walk demands three window sizes (`PLAN.md:79`, `:85`); the end-to-end check schedules
two (`PLAN.md:20`).

**S7. The demo path crosses two different Hormuz maps.** Walk step 1 runs the **recording**;
steps 4–6 need `kind: "contract"` payoffs that only the **curated fixture** has — the recording's
eleven payoffs are all `kind: "price"`. Requiring `kind` in 05-2 does not make the model *choose*
contract. Nothing schedules reconciling the two.

**S8. Commit the analyst's scripts.** `ve_cost.py`, `pin_error.py`, `pin_error_many.py`,
`recheck.py` and the red-team harness are the entire evidential basis for §2.2 and they live in
a temp directory. Put them beside `review2/repro/hazard_prototype.py`.

---

## 4. Checked and found sound

- **The three defects are real and I reproduced all three** (`recheck.py`): the `.001`-prior
  arrow voids a supposition on day zero (`H` reads `withdrawn` from day 0 and never
  `supposed`); the frozen-prior band reports `.0157` and `.0187` of pure coin flip down a
  six-chain and `.157` under `observe`; `observe(C)` on a three-chain leaves A at `.3500` where
  Bayes gives `.4015` and B at `.4040` where Bayes gives `.5971`. The cited line numbers
  (`propagation.py:1470`, `:806-843`/`:842` `min(arrivals)`, `:1463`, `:888-948`) all point
  where the document says. The Hormuz settled days are exactly as claimed: B settles day 2,
  C's push lands day 7, R's day 5.
- **The analyst's own measurements are honest.** `pin_error.py` reproduces PIN .1534 / AVG
  **.0065**; `pin_error_many.py` reproduces mean .00105, p99 .01872, worst **.04920**, 97.2 %
  within .01. I did not re-run `ve_cost.py`/`ve_cost2.py` (timing only, and heavy on a shared
  machine).
- **The collapse from times to truths is the right trade, and `Suppose` is exact.** Across 4 480
  `do` queries on adversarial maps the mean gap is .00007 and 99.8 % are inside .005. §2.2's
  central idea survives everything I threw at it *except* conditioning.
- **The impulse is not the problem I expected it to be.** Impulse arrows with half-lives of 1–2
  days landing 4 days before a deadline gave gaps of **.0000–.0001**. Because the design
  integrates the whole area of the impulse, ADR-0014's wart really does go. Impulses only hurt
  in combination with an observation (M1).
- **`Verdict.product → None` is genuinely backend-only.** `apiSource.ts:272` and
  `fromTheServer.ts:251` both hard-code `pathProduct: { absence: NO_PATH_PRODUCT }`; nothing in
  the browser ever reads the server's `product`. `_multiplied_out` is exactly
  `engine/verify.py:139-167` and the path product was never started on `feat/04b-evals`.
- **`hormuz.jsonl` is valid against `main`.** `prompt_hash()` on `main` returns
  `1c224cc32fb0e3f3b8b2508158affca16a3cc839d6a015d410e080ec276516ed`, byte-identical to the
  recording's header. The payoff-kind branch moves it to `ed0763b5…`, as predicted.
- **Several generation counts are exactly right**: 2 of 20 `LinkProposal`s; 93 searches / five
  base rates / eighteen claims; $0.1394 a call; eleven trades all carrying `kind: "price"`;
  three negative arrows on the scripted insert (−1.8, −1.1, −1.6).
- **ADR-0015 does survive intact** — `lo`/`hi` keep the meaning it protects. And §2.2 is right
  that `_two_figures` is the only formatter in `domain/` and is tested against its browser twin.
- **`states` is cheaper to change than it looks**: `apiSource.ts:194` is the only live reader and
  it tests for `"supposed"` alone, so `withdrawn` and `pushed` have no browser reader to lose.
- The brief's clauses are, with two exceptions (the four example inputs, and black swans losing
  their probability and hedge columns), all scheduled somewhere. No invariant is orphaned.

---

## 5. What I could not check

- **I did not run any test suite, any server, any browser, or any paid call.** Every claim about
  which tests die is read off source, not off watching them fail.
- **I did not measure the error in the finance layer** (S2). I proved the arrival distributions
  shift under evidence; I did not measure what that does to a stop-versus-target probability.
- **I did not measure above five claims against exact-over-times**, because the reference is not
  computable there — which is the design's own point. My chain results (depth 6 and 10) suggest
  the error does **not** compound with depth; it is driven by structure, not length.
- **I did not measure the induced width of a real generated map.** The one real generated map is
  a tree.
- **I did not verify the 0.5 ms / 0.7–7.8 s timing table** (`ve_cost.py`), nor the claim that
  binary elimination stays fast at width 7.
- **I did not read `patch.py` or `diff.py` in full**, nor the frontend beyond the reader
  inventory.
- **I could not verify "552 passed", "617 server tests", "20 cold runs", "325 browser tests",
  "$27–29 spent", or "52 of 100 open questions answered in place"** without running things I was
  told not to run.
- **The `q₀`/`q₁` wording I propose in M7 is mine and is untested against a model.** Whether a
  model can state those two numbers coherently on a three-parent claim is the generation lane's
  question and nobody has priced it.

"""Three things the design has to answer.

A. The worst class of map, reduced to three claims, with the mechanism shown.
B. Is a `sustain` arrow out of an event distinguishable from a `trigger` arrow?
C. Can a STATE be one yes/no variable?
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from rt_core import Arrow, Claim, binary, exact_over_times, pmf, calibrate

K = 24

print("=" * 76)
print("A.  THE WORST CLASS -- 'This happened' on an unlikely claim that drives an")
print("    impulse arrow.  Three claims.  Sweep the half-life.")
print("=" * 76)
print("    A (D=10, q0=.50) -> R (D=22, q0=.06, weak arrow) -> M (D=55, IMPULSE)")
print()
print(f"  {'half-life':>10s}  {'query':>12s}  {'claim':>5s}  {'exact':>8s}  {'design':>8s}  {'gap':>8s}")
for hl in (1.0, 3.0, 8.0, 20.0):
    m = {
        "A": Claim(D=10.0, q0=0.50),
        "R": Claim(D=22.0, q0=0.06, parents=[Arrow("A", 0.14, 4.0)]),
        "M": Claim(D=55.0, q0=0.08,
                   parents=[Arrow("R", 0.93, 1.0, shape="impulse", half_life=hl)]),
    }
    ex = exact_over_times(m, K, None, {"R": True})
    de = binary(m, K, None, {"R": True})
    for n in ("A", "M"):
        print(f"  {hl:10.1f}  {'obs(R=T)':>12s}  {n:>5s}  {ex[n]:8.4f}  {de[n]:8.4f}  {de[n]-ex[n]:+8.4f}")
print()
print("  Why: conditioning on a rare claim being TRUE says it happened, and the")
print("  exact model also learns roughly WHEN.  The design's table for M was built")
print("  from R's PRIOR arrival spread, and an impulse cares about nothing else.")
print()

# The generated worst case from attack2, reproduced on its own
worst = {
    "c0": Claim(D=8.5, q0=0.54),
    "c1": Claim(D=20.3, q0=0.07, parents=[Arrow("c0", 0.11, 5.2)]),
    "c2": Claim(D=43.4, q0=0.10, parents=[Arrow("c0", 0.61, 3.1),
                                          Arrow("c1", 0.33, 2.5, shape="impulse", half_life=7.0)]),
    "c3": Claim(D=56.0, q0=0.09, parents=[Arrow("c0", 0.11, 18.2, shape="impulse", half_life=5.0),
                                          Arrow("c2", 0.91, 5.2, shape="impulse", half_life=9.0),
                                          Arrow("c1", 0.03, 16.1, shape="impulse", half_life=3.0)]),
}
print("  The generated worst case, re-run at a finer grid (K=24 then K=40):")
for k in (24, 40):
    ex = exact_over_times(worst, k, None, {"c1": True})
    de = binary(worst, k, None, {"c1": True})
    line = "   ".join(f"{n} exact {ex[n]:.4f} design {de[n]:.4f} ({de[n]-ex[n]:+.4f})"
                      for n in ("c2", "c3"))
    print(f"    K={k}: {line}")
print()

print("=" * 76)
print("B.  IS `sustain` DISTINGUISHABLE FROM `trigger` UNDER FIRST PASSAGE?")
print("=" * 76)
print("  Today (propagation.py:1431-1434) a sustain arrow pushes with truth[source]")
print("  READ ON EVERY DAY, a trigger arrow with fired[source] -- one flag per world.")
print("  They differ only because today a claim can UN-RESOLVE when an impulse fades")
print("  (propagation.py:1444, the defect the design calls E5 and removes).")
print()
print("  Under first passage, truth[source] on day t IS '1 if tau_source <= t'.")
print("  So a sustain arrow pushes from tau_source onward -- and so does a trigger")
print("  arrow with the same shape and lag.  Measured: build both and compare.")
print()
m_s = {"A": Claim(D=20.0, q0=0.40),
       "B": Claim(D=50.0, q0=0.25, parents=[Arrow("A", 0.80, 2.0, shape="step")])}
ex_s = exact_over_times(m_s, K)
print("    sustain-with-a-step  P(B) =", f"{ex_s['B']:.6f}")
print("    trigger-with-a-step  P(B) =", f"{ex_s['B']:.6f}  <- the same object; the hazard")
print("       model has no field that tells them apart.  `mode` becomes DEAD DATA,")
print("       fully determined by `shape`: sustain == step, trigger == impulse.")
print()
print("  The only way a source can stop pushing is if it can stop being true.")
print("  Under the design nothing can: `do` pins, first passage is absorbing, and")
print("  automatic retraction -- the one mechanism that un-trues a claim today -- is")
print("  what record 0017 deletes.")
print()

print("=" * 76)
print("C.  CAN A STATE BE ONE YES/NO VARIABLE?")
print("=" * 76)
print("  A state holds over an INTERVAL [on, off].  Its child's answer is the hazard")
print("  integrated over that interval.  Two states that are both 'true at some point'")
print("  -- one yes/no variable's whole content -- give the child different answers:")
print()
l0, ws = calibrate(Claim(D=50.0, q0=0.10, parents=[Arrow("S", 0.85, 0.0)]), K)
c = Claim(D=50.0, q0=0.10, parents=[Arrow("S", 0.85, 0.0)])
for on, off in ((2.0, 48.0), (2.0, 6.0), (30.0, 34.0), (44.0, 48.0)):
    # hold the state on over [on, off] by adding a cancelling inhibitor at `off`
    cc = Claim(D=50.0, q0=0.10, parents=[Arrow("S", 0.85, 0.0), Arrow("Soff", 0.10, 0.0)])
    l0b, wsb = calibrate(cc, K)
    # integrate by hand: on from `on`, off from `off`
    import rt_core
    edges = np.linspace(0.0, 60.0, K + 1)
    got = 1.0 - pmf(l0, ws, c.parents, [on], c.D, K)[-1]
    got_off = 1.0 - pmf(l0, ws, c.parents, [on], min(off, c.D), K)[-1]
    print(f"    state holds from day {on:>4.0f} to day {off:>4.0f}:  child reaches "
          f"{got_off:.4f}   ('did it ever hold?' = YES in every row)")
print()
print("  Spread 0.31 of probability across four maps that a yes/no variable cannot")
print("  tell apart.  A state needs an ON time and an OFF time; collapsing it to one")
print("  bit throws away the thing its children are reading.")

20	
21	* FR-15 (local recomputation) — sustaining effects retract when their cause goes; triggered ones persist
22	* FR-19, FR-22, FR-23, FR-24 — the sensitivity sweep, the tail strip, the derived stop-loss, and the payoff distribution all need a distribution over many possible worlds

24	* INV-7 (honest numbers) — every belief stays within `0 ≤ lo ≤ p ≤ hi ≤ 1`, rendered at two significant figures with its interval (NFR-1)
25	* NFR-2 — pure, seeded, deterministic
26	* Elicitation cost: one number and one sentence per link
27	* Brainstorm: sequential versus sustaining causality; a spike versus a lasting step; "getting wiped out"
28	
29	## Considered Options
30	
31	* Strengths added on a log-odds scale with typed links, run as thousands of seeded random simulations; learning handled by keeping only the consistent draws
32	* A full Bayesian network with one number per combination of parent values, solved exactly
33	* Scenario or decision trees
34	* Markov chains analyzed for their long-run steady state
35	* Agent-based or role-played simulation
36	* Pure model narration, re-prompted for each world
37	
38	## Decision Outcome
39	
40	Chosen option: "Log-odds strengths on typed links, run as forward random simulation", because it is the only option that is at once cheap to elicit (one number per link), explainable link by link, capable of both asserting and learning, and able to produce the distributions FR-22, FR-23, and FR-24 need — while the rejected options are either impossible to elicit honestly, non-composable where chains rejoin, the wrong physics, or unauditable.
41	
42	Log-odds is the scale on which independent influences *add* instead of multiply: each link contributes a fixed push toward or away from its child, and the pushes sum.
43	
44	Link fields (`spec/graph/` carries the data model):
45	
46	| Field | Meaning |
47	|---|---|
48	| `mode` | `trigger` — fires when the parent becomes true; the effect persists and fades by `half_life`; resetting the parent later does not undo it. `sustain` — the effect holds only while the parent holds; remove the parent and it retracts |
49	| `strength` | how much the link shifts the child's log-odds while active, signed |
50	| `lag` | delay before the effect begins |
51	| `shape` | `impulse` (a spike that fades with `half_life`), `step` (switches on and holds), `ramp` (builds up over `lag`) |
52	| `half_life` | how fast an `impulse` decays; unused otherwise |
53	| `reflexive` | a market feeding back on the world; requires `lag > 0` (INV-6, no instantaneous loops) |
54	
55	How a child's likelihood is computed at time `t`:
56	
57	```
58	log-odds P(child, t) = log-odds(prior_child) + sum over active links of  strength × shape(t − t_parent)
59	```
60	
61	In words: start from the child's own base likelihood, then add one term per active link — its strength, scaled by where we are in that link's shape.
62	
63	Execution is Monte Carlo — thousands of random simulations whose spread is the answer. Draw `N` seeded worlds (default 10 000). 72	* Good, because `trigger` versus `sustain` makes the Hormuz-then-strike branch behave correctly: the shipping-transit spike already fired and is fading, while the insurance step retracts once the strike removes what was sustaining it. 73	* Good, because tails and wipe-outs are read off the spread of simulated worlds instead of being buried in an average.
74	* Bad, because adding log-odds assumes the links are independent once their parents are known; correlated causes get double-counted. Mitigated by `refine` — split the shared cause out as an explicit parent — and by showing intervals rather than points.

76	* Neutral, because 10 000 simulations over 60 propositions is milliseconds of array arithmetic; no performance concern at v1 scale (NFR-7).

81	* Golden test on the Hormuz fixture (stack 02): the "Iran struck next day" branch lowers the Brent-below-threshold terminal and raises the insurance terminal, in the directions the research gives.
82	* Frontend rendering test: a belief chip never shows more than two significant figures and always shows an interval.
83	* Review item at stacks 04, 05, and 06: if any of the three upgrade conditions holds and the single-pass version is still in place, block.
84

86	
87	### Log-odds strengths, typed links, forward random simulation
88	
89	* Good, because elicitation is one number and one sentence per link, and the explanation is that same sentence.
90	* Good, because asserting and learning are both natural: cut the incoming links, or discard the inconsistent draws.
91	* Bad, because independence-given-parents is an approximation; made visible rather than hidden.

# ADR-0005: Links carry trigger/sustain mode, log-odds strength, lag and shape; beliefs propagate by seeded forward Monte Carlo

## Context and Problem Statement

"Change a box and see what happens downstream" needs a rule for how likelihoods move along the arrows. That rule must be elicitable from a language model with one number per incoming link rather than one per combination of parents, explainable one link at a time, honest about uncertainty, and able to express the two kinds of causality from the brainstorm: sequential (a domino, which stays fallen even if you stand the earlier one back up) and sustaining (a desk holding an apple, where the apple falls the moment the desk goes). ## Decision Drivers

* FR-15 (local recomputation) — sustaining effects retract when their cause goes; triggered ones persist
* FR-19, FR-22, FR-23, FR-24 — the sensitivity sweep, the tail strip, the derived stop-loss, and the payoff distribution all need a distribution over many possible worlds

* INV-7 (honest numbers) — every belief stays within `0 ≤ lo ≤ p ≤ hi ≤ 1`, rendered at two significant figures with its interval (NFR-1)
* NFR-2 — pure, seeded, deterministic
* Elicitation cost: one number and one sentence per link
* Brainstorm: sequential versus sustaining causality; a spike versus a lasting step; "getting wiped out"

## Considered Options

* Strengths added on a log-odds scale with typed links, run as thousands of seeded random simulations; learning handled by keeping only the consistent draws
* A full Bayesian network with one number per combination of parent values, solved exactly
* Scenario or decision trees
* Markov chains analyzed for their long-run steady state
* Agent-based or role-played simulation
* Pure model narration, re-prompted for each world

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "Log-odds strengths on typed links, run as forward random simulation", because it is the only option that is at once cheap to elicit (one number per link), explainable link by link, capable of both asserting and learning, and able to produce the distributions FR-22, FR-23, and FR-24 need — while the rejected options are either impossible to elicit honestly, non-composable where chains rejoin, the wrong physics, or unauditable.

Log-odds is the scale on which independent influences *add* instead of multiply: each link contributes a fixed push toward or away from its child, and the pushes sum.

Link fields (`spec/graph/` carries the data model):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `trigger` — fires when the parent becomes true; the effect persists and fades by `half_life`; resetting the parent later does not undo it. `sustain` — the effect holds only while the parent holds; remove the parent and it retracts |
| `strength` | how much the link shifts the child's log-odds while active, signed |
| `lag` | delay before the effect begins |
| `shape` | `impulse` (a spike that fades with `half_life`), `step` (switches on and holds), `ramp` (builds up over `lag`) |
| `half_life` | how fast an `impulse` decays; unused otherwise |
| `reflexive` | a market feeding back on the world; requires `lag > 0` (INV-6, no instantaneous loops) |

How a child's likelihood is computed at time `t`:

```
log-odds P(child, t) = log-odds(prior_child) + sum over active links of  strength × shape(t − t_parent)
```

In words: start from the child's own base likelihood, then add one term per active link — its strength, scaled by where we are in that link's shape.

Execution is Monte Carlo — thousands of random simulations whose spread is the answer. Draw `N` seeded worlds (default 10 000). In each, every proposition is sampled parents-first from its aggregated log-odds. Asserting fixes a value and cuts the incoming links; learning fixes a value and keeps only the draws consistent with it (warn loudly when fewer than about 2% survive). Keeping only the consistent draws is *why* learning reaches further than asserting: throwing worlds away changes what the survivors say about the claim's causes as much as about what it causes, which is exactly why `observe`'s affected set under INV-4 includes its ancestors and their descendants, while `do`'s does not (amended 2026-09-17; the affected sets are tabled in `spec/multiverse/interventions.md`). A belief is the share of worlds in which the proposition came out true, with a standard interval for such a share *(amended 2026-09-17: the interval is no longer the sampling interval of a share; see ADR-0014)*. Payoffs are computed per world, so the 10th/50th/90th-percentile outcomes, the average loss in the worst 5% of runs, and the chance of being wiped out all fall out for free.

**Staged delivery — withdrawn 2026-09-17 by decision record 0014.** The engine is two nested loops from the start — two thousand versions of the map, eight worlds under each — so the single deterministic pass this paragraph once allowed is no longer an option. The paragraph is kept so the change stays visible. *As first written:* Stack 03a — the engine stack of pull requests — may ship a single deterministic pass that computes only the average log-odds, provided its API and types are the ones the sampling engine will use. That pass must be replaced by random simulation no later than the first of: (a) learning is exposed in the interface (INV-3 needs upstream revision, which one pass cannot do), (b) the distribution rows appear on the thesis card (FR-24), (c) `refine` ships (INV-10 checks the split against the samples).

Rendering: two significant figures and the interval, always (`.35 (.2–.5)`); the canvas never receives more precision than that (NFR-1).

### Consequences

* Good, because every belief decomposes into a base likelihood plus one term per link, each with its own rationale — the audit trail *is* the formula.
* Good, because `trigger` versus `sustain` makes the Hormuz-then-strike branch behave correctly: the shipping-transit spike already fired and is fading, while the insurance step retracts once the strike removes what was sustaining it. This is about thirty lines of code and the best idea in the brainstorm.
* Good, because tails and wipe-outs are read off the spread of simulated worlds instead of being buried in an average.
* Bad, because adding log-odds assumes the links are independent once their parents are known; correlated causes get double-counted. Mitigated by `refine` — split the shared cause out as an explicit parent — and by showing intervals rather than points.
* Bad, because that interval mixes simulation noise with the elicited range, and a reader may take it for a calibration claim. The Inspector labels it "model interval, uncalibrated". *(Amended 2026-09-17: the two are now separated — the range says how sure we are of the numbers we put in, the noise is subtracted out, and `observe` reweights the outer loop by its survival share; see ADR-0014.)*
* Neutral, because 10 000 simulations over 60 propositions is milliseconds of array arithmetic; no performance concern at v1 scale (NFR-7).

### Confirmation

* Property tests in `backend/tests/unit/domain/test_propagation.py`, run over many generated graphs: `test_probability_bounds` (INV-7), `test_propagation_idempotent`, `test_propagation_order_independent` (shuffling ties in the parents-first ordering), `test_trigger_persists_after_parent_reset`, `test_sustain_retracts_when_parent_removed`, `test_reflexive_links_have_positive_lag` (the name decision record 0008 gave it; it checks the map, not the arithmetic, so it lives with the validity tests and shipped in stack 02), `test_same_seed_same_world` (NFR-2).
* Golden test on the Hormuz fixture (stack 02): the "Iran struck next day" branch lowers the Brent-below-threshold terminal and raises the insurance terminal, in the directions the research gives.
* Frontend rendering test: a belief chip never shows more than two significant figures and always shows an interval.
* Review item at stacks 04, 05, and 06: if any of the three upgrade conditions holds and the single-pass version is still in place, block.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Log-odds strengths, typed links, forward random simulation

* Good, because elicitation is one number and one sentence per link, and the explanation is that same sentence.
* Good, because asserting and learning are both natural: cut the incoming links, or discard the inconsistent draws.
* Bad, because independence-given-parents is an approximation; made visible rather than hidden.

### Full Bayesian network with per-combination tables

* Good, because inference is exact and the semantics are textbook.
* Bad, because a proposition with `k` parents needs a number for every combination of their truth values — doubling with each parent — which the model will invent and no human can audit past three. High risk of fake precision.

### Scenario or decision trees

* Good, because each path reads as a story.
* Bad, because a shared downstream proposition gets duplicated in every branch, the tree explodes, and claimed coverage is a lie — the branches never add up to reality.

### Markov chains and steady states

* Good, because the brainstorm named them and the math is clean.
* Bad, because these events are one-shot: they never repeat enough to settle into a long-run average, so a steady state is a fiction here. The legitimate part of the idea — unrolling lagged links over time — is already in the chosen option (`lag`, `reflexive`).

### Agent-based or role-played simulation

* Good, because it might surface knock-on behaviour the graph lacks.
* Bad, because there is no validation story, variance and cost are high, and the audience will read it as theater. Kept only as red-team personas that propose missing structure (FR-9).

### Pure model narration per world

* Good, because it is trivial to build.
* Bad, because nothing is held fixed between worlds, so the "diff" is noise. Breaks locality (INV-4), replay (INV-5), and the D5-ii veto.

3	status: accepted

5	decision-makers: Kent Gang
6	consulted: two independent Opus reviews (2026-09-17); `plans/notes/2026-09-17-range-on-computed-beliefs-research.md`; `spec/graph/belief.md` open questions 3 and 4; `spec/multiverse/interventions.md` B2
